clue.text: Prophet's haste to halve the workload

parts.note: Job is the Old Testament prophet famed for patience; with the possessive he gives a run of four letters
to hare is to rush along with great speed, so haste stands for that word

explanation.surface: A prophet in a hurry looks for a way to cut his work in half.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'Prophet's' is part of the letters, not a link: JOB'S, then HARE for haste.
explanation.definitionFit: Two employees sharing one post each do half the work, an arrangement that halves the load for each.

clue.text: In old car, Jack always cut in

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for jack in playing cards

indicators.note: the word for cut goes inside the word for always

parts.note: ay is an old or poetic word for always
to lop is to cut off

explanation.surface: In an old car, a man named Jack keeps pruning things.
explanation.walkthrough: AY (also spelt aye) meaning 'ever' is an old word crosswords use often.
explanation.definitionFit: A dilapidated old motor car is called a jalopy, an informal word.

clue.text: Opening fish in endless spell of overindulgence

indicators.note: the fish goes inside the shortened word
without its end, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a binge is a bout of excess
a roach is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A fish is cut open during a never-ending eating bout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opening' looks like an adjective or noun but means starting a discussion; 'endless' drops the final letter of the binge word.
explanation.definitionFit: Broaching a subject is opening it for discussion, as broaching a cask opens it.

clue.text: Rumour has it corn seeds are included in the grass

indicators.note: the seed heads are placed within the dried grass word

parts.note: hay is dried grass
ears of corn are the seed-bearing heads of the plant

explanation.surface: Gossip says that grain has got mixed into the grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has it' is a link, as in 'rumour has it'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearsay is information heard from others and not verified, which is what rumour is.

clue.text: Perhaps writing poem on love for competition

indicators.note: in a down clue, placed on top of the letter for love

parts.note: writing is one of the three Rs, reading, writing and arithmetic, hence R
an ode is a lyric poem
love is zero in tennis, hence O

explanation.surface: Maybe someone writes a love poem to enter a contest.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'three Rs' are reading, writing and (a)rithmetic, so 'writing' can be R; 'Perhaps' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A rodeo is a contest of cowboy skills such as riding broncos, so it is a competition.

clue.text: Trouble is dogging new dish

indicators.note: something dogging another follows close behind it, so these letters come after the abbreviation for new

parts.note: ado is fuss or bother, a trouble
taken as written

explanation.surface: A worry is hanging over some novel food someone has served.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dish' is not food here but slang for a very attractive person.
explanation.definitionFit: A dish is informal slang for a handsome person, and the Greek youth's name is used for any good-looking man.

clue.text: Function with animal doctor entertaining company in bird sanctuary

parts.note: a do is a party or social function

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to hold them, so the vet word goes round the company word

parts.note: a vet treats animals

explanation.surface: At a party a vet has guests in a place for birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' is a link; 'entertaining' is a container signal, the vet playing host to the company.
explanation.definitionFit: A dovecot is a shelter for doves or pigeons, a refuge for birds.

clue.text: Bread not available for granny

parts.note: naan or nan is Indian flatbread

explanation.surface: Grandma finds there is no bread left.
explanation.walkthrough: NAN is a spelling of naan, the Indian flatbread.
explanation.definitionFit: Nanna is an affectionate word for a grandmother.

clue.text: The map is unrolled by another member of the crew

indicators.note: a map unrolled is spread out of its folded shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sailor unrolls the chart for a fellow crewman.
explanation.definitionFit: A shipmate is a fellow sailor on the same ship, another of the crew.

clue.text: Probably I had always to accept God

indicators.note: the run of the other pieces takes in the god's name

parts.note: I'd is the contraction of I had
ay is an old word for always
Ares is the Greek god of war

explanation.surface: Perhaps I always had to take on a god.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to accept' means the pieces for 'I had' and 'always' open up to take in the Greek war god.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means I suppose or very likely, a hedge equivalent to probably.

clue.text: Vindaloo and rice cooked by an artist …

indicators.note: food that is cooked is altered from its raw state, so these three words are rearranged

parts.note: all fifteen letters of the three words, including the joining word, form the pool

explanation.surface: Someone prepares a curry dinner with rice for a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: Unusually the word 'and' is part of the fodder: its letters are needed to make up fifteen.
explanation.definitionFit: The Renaissance painter of the Mona Lisa is the example of an artist meant; the ellipsis leads into the next clue.

clue.text: … and another idiot, in good company

parts.note: PI, short for pious, is the crossword abbreviation for good

indicators.note: the fool's word is placed inside the run formed by the other two pieces

parts.note: an ass is a foolish person

explanation.surface: Continuing from the previous clue, a second painter is called a fool in pleasant society.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the preceding clue: 'another' means another artist, like the one just named.
explanation.definitionFit: Following on from the previous clue's painter, this is another famous artist, the Spanish cubist.

clue.text: Playground locals at first intend to bring under cultivation

parts.note: rec, short for recreation ground, is a British word for a public playground

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word locals is taken

parts.note: to aim is to intend

explanation.surface: Neighbourhood residents plan to turn the local playground into farmland.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'rec' is the British short form for a recreation ground or park.
explanation.definitionFit: To reclaim land is to make waste or flooded ground fit for farming again.

clue.text: Man faced with an uphill task when his pussy's lost

definitions.text: Man faced with an uphill task

indicators.note: something lost is astray or disordered, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: the letters of the two words, the possessive ending counted as a plain letter s

explanation.surface: A man has a hard climb ahead of him once his cat has gone missing.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth this king was condemned to push a boulder up a hill forever, only for it to roll back down.
explanation.definitionFit: The mythical king punished by endlessly rolling a rock uphill is the archetype of a man with a hopeless uphill labour.

clue.text: Retreat from skin game

parts.note: a hide is an animal's skin
an away game is one played at the opponents' ground, so away stands for game

explanation.surface: Hunters withdraw from skinning their quarry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' looks like quarry, but stands for AWAY, as in an away game.
explanation.definitionFit: A hideaway is a secluded refuge, a retreat.

clue.text: Crime article required by newspaper

parts.note: the definite article is the word the
FT is the Financial Times, a British newspaper

explanation.surface: A newspaper needs a crime story.
explanation.walkthrough: FT is the Financial Times, the British business paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealing is a criminal offence, so it is a straightforward example of a crime.

clue.text: Knowledge apparent in issue covering sport

indicators.note: the issue word goes round the sport abbreviation

parts.note: an edition is an issue of a publication
RU is Rugby Union, a sport

explanation.surface: A magazine number covering sport shows its learning.
explanation.walkthrough: RU (Rugby Union) is a frequent crossword abbreviation for a sport. 'apparent in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Erudition is deep learning acquired by study, a scholarly kind of knowledge.

clue.text: Antique household implement novice employed in tart

indicators.note: the beginner's word is placed within the pastry word

parts.note: a flan is an open tart
a tiro, or tyro, is a beginner

explanation.surface: A beginner is put to work making a pie with an old kitchen tool.
explanation.walkthrough: TIRO (also tyro) is a learner.
explanation.definitionFit: Before electric irons, a flat iron heated on the stove was used for pressing clothes.

clue.text: Pane of glass weighing relatively little

definitions.meaning: a window pane is called by this word, especially in a leaded or mullioned window

explanation.definitionFit: The same word names a single window pane and means having little weight, two unrelated senses.

clue.text: Dash round Queen's houses

indicators.note: the dash word goes round the monarch's letters

parts.note: a dash is a small amount, a trace
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: Someone rushes around the Queen's residences.
explanation.walkthrough: ER (Elizabeth Regina) is a standard crossword Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrace is a row of joined houses, so the word names a set of houses.

clue.text: Failing to play a part in housework

definitions.meaning: an actor who forgets lines on stage is said to do this
wiping washed dishes with a tea towel, a domestic chore

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both forgetting one's lines in a play and the chore of wiping dishes after washing.

clue.text: The competition is mounting — it's up to clubs showing favouritism

indicators.note: in a down clue, mounting means rising, so the word is read upwards

parts.note: an open is a golf or tennis tournament open to all

indicators.note: in a down clue, up reads the word bottom to top

parts.note: the word it, the apostrophe ending not counted
C is the abbreviation for clubs in cards

explanation.surface: Contest results are rising and a bias in favour of insiders is the cause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is mounting' turns OPEN to NEPO and 'up' turns IT to TI; 'to' joins on C. 'The' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Nepotic means practising nepotism, favouritism to relatives in appointments.

clue.text: Feel aggrieved by pence being deducted from grant

indicators.note: the coin's letter is taken out of the giving word

parts.note: to present something is to grant or give it

explanation.surface: Someone is bitter at having money docked from their grant.
explanation.definitionFit: To resent something is to feel bitterness or indignation about it.

clue.text: Retired worker employed around state guest-house

indicators.note: the reversed insect word is placed round the verb for state
to retire is to go back, so the insect word is turned backwards

parts.note: a worker is a worker ant, the crossword's usual insect
to aver is to state firmly

explanation.surface: A pensioner has been taken on at a guest-house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired' turns the insect backwards, and 'around' puts it round the verb for state; 'employed' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A Greek taverna is a small inn or eating house, loosely a guest-house.

clue.text: Bomb attached to vehicle by cleric

parts.note: the V1, written here as VI, was the German flying bomb of the Second World War
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A churchman has a bomb fixed to his car.
explanation.walkthrough: The V1 'doodlebug' was a German flying bomb; crosswords write it VI.
explanation.definitionFit: A vicar is a parish priest in the Church of England, a cleric.

clue.text: Beef about editor, I see

indicators.note: turned about means turned round, so the whole run is read backwards

parts.note: to spot is to see

explanation.surface: Someone complains about the editor and says they understand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns the whole run EDISPOT backwards. 'Beef' looks like a verb (complain), but it is the meat.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a cut of beef from the upper hindquarter, used for roasting.

clue.text: Note heard from bell

indicators.note: the word for the banknote is said aloud

parts.note: a tenner is a ten-pound banknote

explanation.surface: A musical note rings out from a bell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' suggests music but is a banknote: a tenner is a British ten-pound note.
explanation.definitionFit: In bell-ringing the tenor is the largest and lowest-pitched bell of a ring.

clue.text: Nation opposing the enemy, with speed the essence here

parts.note: a race is a people or nation
against means in opposition to
time is the enemy, as the saying has it

explanation.surface: A country fighting its foe, where quick action is vital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time is the enemy' is a set phrase, so 'the enemy' gives TIME.
explanation.definitionFit: A struggle to finish before a deadline is a situation where speed is essential.

clue.text: Snow's covering surface of road, causing some anxiety

indicators.note: the snow word goes round the other piece

parts.note: a névé is granular snow on a glacier; the possessive gives the plural ending

indicators.note: only the top letter of the word road is taken

explanation.surface: Snow has settled on the road, making drivers jittery.
explanation.walkthrough: NÉVÉ is hard granular snow on a glacier; NEVES goes round R, the first letter of 'road'.
explanation.definitionFit: Feelings of nervousness or apprehension are called nerves, a form of anxiety.

clue.text: Dissolute prince taken to court by American police division

indicators.note: dissolute means loose or debauched, signalling that the letters run loose

explanation.surface: A debauched royal is sued in an American court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken to' simply sets CT after the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: In US cities the police force is split into districts, each called by this word.
